research_rationale:
EO 11962 (42 FR 4323, January 19, 1977; held official Federal Register text) established the President's Advisory Board on International Investment and its supporting duties, with its own sunset of December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended. EO 12007 of August 22, 1977 terminated the Board (section 5(a)) and revoked EO 11962 (section 5(b), "(b ) Executive Order No. 11962 of January 19, 1977, is revoked."), which is earlier than the own-terms sunset. Every clause therefore ended on 1977-08-22 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The inventory is corrected to add section 1(a), omitted by the machine segmentation. The held U.S. Code note at 22 U.S.C. 3107 says EO 11962 was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12007, Aug. 22, 1977, 42 F.R. 42839, which agrees.

No amendment, extension or earlier termination of the Board appears in the held sources. Section 6 of EO 12007 supersedes subsections of EO 11948 that extended other committees to December 31, 1978; it does not concern EO 11962 and does not extend it.","independent_command_check":"The supporting commands (the Executive Director's staff and administrative services, the Executive Secretary appointment, the Federal Advisory Committee Act functions performed by the Executive Director, member compensation) all exist only for the Board and are within the revoked order; none is a free-standing command that survives the Board's termination.","savings_check":"EO 12007 contains no savings clause (sections 1 to 6 read). Section 6 of EO 12007 supersedes parts of EO 11948 only. Appointments under EO 11962 were limited to the remaining life of the Board, and the Board was terminated, so none survives; the statute the Board advised under, the International Investment Survey Act of 1976, is a separate matter that the order did not enact.","scope_check":"EO 12007 revokes EO 11962 as a whole by number and date and separately terminates the Board; no part is excepted. The machine inventory missed section 1(a); the corrected inventory has nine clauses covering every operative sentence between the preamble and the signature, and each is ended by the same instrument."}
